text:
mike: ACME reporting sustained 429s on their Dedicated pool 'nyc-gold' since ~09:12 UTC. They say traffic is normal but token rate dropped. Ticket #4567.

acme-sre: saw spikes of 429 for ~15m, then partial success. response headers: `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`, `x-pool: bronze-1` (we expected nyc-gold). Pls confirm.

mike: quick repro I ran: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "X-Tier: gold" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` -> 429 + `x-pool: bronze-1`.

nina: looking at control-plane routing logs. initial request arrives with header `X-Tier: ["gold"]` (proxy upstream sends arrays for single-value headers). our router's matcher expects a string equality on `gold` so it fell through to fallback policy which mapped to bronze pool.

nina: snippet from routing trace:
```
incoming_headers: {"X-Tier": "[\"gold\"]"}
routing_policy: tier == "gold" -> pool nyc-gold
match_result: false -> apply fallthrough -> pool bronze-1
```

omar: that explains autoscaler behavior. bronze-1 hit its concurrency SLO -> autoscaler for bronze did scale but we have small headroom; because traffic was misrouted we exhausted bronze capacity and hit throttles. nyc-gold never got the load so its autoscaler didn't act.

lisa: CC'ing cust-success so they know we're on it :eyes:

deploy-bot: Incident INC-4567 created, priority P1. Links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4567

mike: customer asked for immediate mitigation. options? quick patch to normalize header parsing in control plane? temporary rule to treat any `X-Tier` that contains the substring "gold" as gold?

nina: quick mitigation deployed to control-plane routing-service in staging: normalize headers by stripping surrounding array chars and whitespace before matching. simple regex applied. will push to prod as hotfix if ops ok.

omar: note: even if routing hotfix goes live, bronze pool is cold-throttled now. plan: 1) push routing hotfix 2) scale bronze pool up to relieve customer requests in the short term 3) reconcile autoscaler policies so they don't scale opposite pool on misroute.

mike: repro steps we gave to customer to validate after fix:
1) flush client proxy cache (some proxies persist header arrays)
2) call generation endpoint with `X-Tier: gold` (or SDK)
3) confirm response header `x-pool: nyc-gold` and 200s

acme-sre: OK will try in ~10m and report back. thanks.

nina: patch rolled to prod control-plane in canary (10% of routing traffic) at 09:35 UTC. monitoring latency and `route_mismatch` metric. currently canary shows correct mapping for incoming array-encoded headers.

mike: ping @omar for scaling bronze-1 temporarily, and @lisa to update the customer with ETA.

omar: manual scale +100 tokens/s to bronze-1 started at 09:40 UTC. also bumped `noisy_neighbor_detection` threshold to avoid premature throttles for the next 20m.

lisa: updated ACME: "We're rolling a routing fix now and temporarily increasing capacity; please retry in ~15m. PM follow-up to come."

acme-sre: retried at 09:51Z — confirmed 200 and `x-pool: nyc-gold`. Looks good from our side. We'll watch for a bit.

nina: follow-ups: (a) add header-normalization to router unit tests, (b) add metric for header-format fallthroughs, (c) recommend SDK change to set single-value headers as plain strings. I'll open tickets.

mike: thanks team. I'll keep INC-4567 open and will craft a short postmortem once we have timeline + root cause. :thumbsup:

acme-sre: appreciate the quick turnaround.
